headline: RU: Suspension recommended for 4 students after attack on journalists
summary: A probe committee has recommended the temporary suspension of four students, including Chhatra Dal leaders, following an assault on journalists at Rajshahi University.
details: A probe committee at Rajshahi University (RU) has recommended the temporary suspension of four students following an attack on journalists at Shaheed Ziaur Rahman Hall.
caption:

headline: DNCC to repaint Metro Rail pillars with July graffiti
summary: The Dhaka North City Corporation will paint portraits of martyrs and leaders of the July uprising, including Khaleda Zia, on pillars from Mirpur-12 to Agargaon.
details: The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) has launched a 'July Graffiti Remake' campaign to repaint Metro Rail pillars from Mirpur-12 to Agargaon.
DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan announced that the pillars will feature portraits of those who were martyred or led the July mass uprising to restore democracy.
The administrator specifically mentioned that Khaleda Zia's portrait will be included due to her significant contribution to the uprising.
The project follows a cleanup drive where political posters, university and coaching center advertisements were removed from the pillars within 72 hours.
Alongside the graffiti, the DNCC is working to clear footpaths from illegal occupation in areas like Mirpur-10 and Hope Market to ensure pedestrian safety.
Administrator Khan emphasized that monitoring teams have been formed to prevent the re-occupation of footpaths and that greening initiatives are adding trees to the cleared spaces.
The administrator also criticized certain political leaders for supporting battery-run auto-rickshaws, alleging some own hundreds of vehicles while claiming to support public demands.
The campaign was officially inaugurated at the Mirpur-10 roundabout, where the administrator painted the 248th pillar to mark the start of the project.
caption:
Metro Rail pillars are getting a makeover. Portraits of July uprising martyrs and leaders will now adorn the city's transit pillars.

The Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) has launched a 'July Graffiti Remake' campaign to repaint Metro Rail pillars from Mirpur-12 to Agargaon.

DNCC Administrator Shafiqul Islam Khan announced that the pillars will feature portraits of those who were martyred or led the July mass uprising to restore democracy.

The administrator specifically mentioned that Khaleda Zia's portrait will be included due to her significant contribution to the uprising.

The project follows a cleanup drive where political posters, university and coaching center advertisements were removed from the pillars within 72 hours.

Alongside the graffiti, the DNCC is working to clear footpaths from illegal occupation in areas like Mirpur-10 and Hope Market to ensure pedestrian safety.

Administrator Khan emphasized that monitoring teams have been formed to prevent the re-occupation of footpaths and that greening initiatives are adding trees to the cleared spaces.

The administrator also criticized certain political leaders for supporting battery-run auto-rickshaws, alleging some own hundreds of vehicles while claiming to support public demands.

The campaign was officially inaugurated at the Mirpur-10 roundabout, where the administrator painted the 248th pillar to mark the start of the project.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo
